newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond issuance expected to take off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond issuance expected to take off.

text.p: Lower financing rates, upcoming market holidays and year's-end just around the corner should prompt corporate bond issuance to take off, dealers said.
"Today's numbers (payrolls) support the decision of the Fed not to tighten so the issuance calendar is going to get heavy starting next week," said one syndicate source.
On Friday, the Labor Department reported the U.S. economy lost 40,000 jobs in the month of September and said the unemployment rate ticked up to 5.2 percent.
Weakness in the closely watched economic indicator prompted several experts to predict the Federal Reserve is likely to keep interest rates steady in the near future.
"No one thinks the Fed's going to tighten," said another syndicate official.
"Many players think today's weak payrolls report is somewhat of an abberation so issuers have been given a window of opportunity to issue debt now while the rate environment is attractive," he added.
Following Friday's payrolls report, U.S. Treasury prices shot up substantially, sending yields to sharply lower levels, making it less costly to finance debt, dealers said.
With an approaching holiday season, issuers will rush to issue debt now rather than face the challenge of trying to structure deals later when dealer's desks are thinly staffed.

"If you'e thinking about issuing debt you may as well do it now," one dealer said. "It starts getting tough toward year-end when you have all these holidays coming up...this is a key time to get paper done."
